evidence.claim: Memorial said 2022 was marked by de facto military censorship, 74 new names were added to the main political-prisoner list, and more than 5,000 administrative cases and 200-plus criminal cases targeted anti-army speech.
evidence.title: Политзаключённые и политические репрессии в России в 2022 году
evidence.excerpt: Memorial said 2022 was marked by de facto military censorship, 74 new names were added to the main political-prisoner list, and more than 5,000 administrative cases and 200-plus criminal cases targeted anti-army speech.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Local-language retrospective report with explicit annual statistics and repression categories.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Putin’s regime because the report describes state repression in response to anti-war speech and public dissent.
contrary_evidence: The report is a retrospective summary and not a contemporaneous government record.

evidence.claim: The Post reports that Russian officials spent weeks denying plans to attack Ukraine, ridiculing warnings as hysteria and fairy tales, before the full-scale assault began.
evidence.title: Russia's attack on Ukraine came after months of denials it would attack
evidence.excerpt: The Post reports that Russian officials spent weeks denying plans to attack Ukraine, ridiculing warnings as hysteria and fairy tales, before the full-scale assault began.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous report summarizing a broad denial campaign immediately contradicted by events.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strong direct attribution to Putin’s governing line, though the article notes some uncertainty about whether the denials were deliberate disinformation or closed decision-making.
contrary_evidence: The article notes it is not clear whether the denials were deliberate disinformation or closed-off decision-making.

evidence.claim: Reuters reports that the International Court of Justice confirmed Ukraine’s case and said Russia’s claim that it invaded to prevent genocide is false.
evidence.title: World Court: Ukraine has filed suit against Russia, citing false genocide claims
evidence.excerpt: Reuters reports that the International Court of Justice confirmed Ukraine’s case and said Russia’s claim that it invaded to prevent genocide is false.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters summary of an ICJ filing and the court’s confirmation; strong corroboration, though still mediated reporting.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strong indirect attribution: the false genocide rationale is Putin’s and Russia’s public justification for the invasion.
contrary_evidence: Russia publicly maintained the genocide justification.

evidence.claim: Putin told business leaders he had no other option but to order the operation against Ukraine and said Moscow had been forced into action.
evidence.title: Putin tells Russian business people he had no choice over Ukraine
evidence.excerpt: Putin told business leaders he had no other option but to order the operation against Ukraine and said Moscow had been forced into action.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct Reuters report on a televised meeting and Putin’s own words.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strong direct attribution: these are Putin’s own public statements explaining the invasion.

evidence.claim: OCCRP said leaked emails showed Sibur spent large sums on Villa Sellgren, a mansion on the Gulf of Finland reported as a Putin vacation destination, and that employees did not understand why the money was being spent.
evidence.title: We Cannot Use It: Leaked E-Mails Show How Russian Petrochemical Giant Sibur Paid For Villa Linked to Putin
evidence.excerpt: OCCRP said leaked emails showed Sibur spent large sums on Villa Sellgren, a mansion on the Gulf of Finland reported as a Putin vacation destination, and that employees did not understand why the money was being spent.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Document-backed investigative reporting with leaked emails and corroborating prior reporting.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within the 2022 target year and tied to a long-running Putin-linked property pattern.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but strong: the property is reported as Putin-linked and the funding flowed through a company long associated with him and his family.
contrary_evidence: The company and associated actors did not publicly explain the spending as ordinary business necessity.

evidence.claim: OCCRP reported that companies with ties to Russia’s security and prosecutorial elite won large state contracts and that watchdogs described this as a common pattern where taxpayers’ money flows to those close to the elite.
evidence.title: Cars, Connections, and Contracts in Putin’s Russia
evidence.excerpt: OCCRP reported that companies with ties to Russia’s security and prosecutorial elite won large state contracts and that watchdogs described this as a common pattern where taxpayers’ money flows to those close to the elite.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Documentary investigative reporting showing a recurring conflict-of-interest pattern in the Putin-era state.
evidence.period_fit: Pre-2022 pattern evidence relevant to the 2022 ruler-period.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but strong: the article situates the contract pattern inside the Putin-era elite network.

evidence.claim: OCCRP published leaked emails showing a memo labeled Objective: Clear Sanctions that described a restructuring plan to preserve the Rotenberg brothers’ share in Helsinki Halli.
evidence.title: Leaked Emails Reveal How Putin’s Friends Dodged Sanctions With Help of Western Enablers
evidence.excerpt: OCCRP published leaked emails showing a memo labeled Objective: Clear Sanctions that described a restructuring plan to preserve the Rotenberg brothers’ share in Helsinki Halli.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct documentary leak with explicit sanctions-evasion planning.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within the 2022 target year, though the conduct is rooted in earlier sanctions circumvention.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but strong: the brothers are long-time Putin associates, and the concealment behavior is tied to Putin’s orbit.
contrary_evidence: The source relies on leaked emails and describes an alleged restructuring plan rather than a judicial finding.

evidence.claim: Treasury said Putin has investments in Gunvor, that the Rotenberg brothers received about $7 billion in contracts awarded by Putin, and that Yuri Kovalchuk was Putin’s personal banker and cashiers-like advisor.
evidence.title: Treasury Sanctions Russian Officials, Members Of The Russian Leadership’s Inner Circle, And An Entity For Involvement In The Situation In Ukraine
evidence.excerpt: Treasury said Putin has investments in Gunvor, that the Rotenberg brothers received about $7 billion in contracts awarded by Putin, and that Yuri Kovalchuk was Putin’s personal banker and cashiers-like advisor.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official sanctions notice with unusually explicit descriptions of the Putin inner circle’s financial and contract links.
evidence.period_fit: Pre-2022 pattern evidence relevant to the 2022 ruler-period.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but strong: the notice directly ties financial benefit, contracts and access to Putin’s personal circle.
contrary_evidence: This is a sanctions finding, not a criminal verdict; the government notice is itself an accusation-based instrument.

evidence.claim: Amnesty said Russian authorities dismantled Navalny’s Anti-Corruption Foundation, labelled his organizations extremist, blocked their websites, and criminalized their activities.
evidence.title: Russia: One year after jailing, Aleksei Navalny and his associates in a living hell
evidence.excerpt: Amnesty said Russian authorities dismantled Navalny’s Anti-Corruption Foundation, labelled his organizations extremist, blocked their websites, and criminalized their activities.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct human-rights reporting on state suppression of an anti-corruption movement with clear, traceable dates and actions.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within the 2022 target year and immediately prior to the invasion period.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strong indirect attribution: the crackdown targeted the leading anti-corruption network challenging Putin’s circle, but the item does not itself prove direct personal orders.
